interest: This file offers a striking intellectual artifact from the early stages of the Second Sino-Japanese War, illustrating how Japanese academic elites rationalized imperial expansion and pan-Asianism through sociological, demographic, and economic theories rather than solely through mystical nationalism. Professor Takata's demographic critique of Western civilization—attributing European decline to declining birth rates, capitalist luxury, and individualism—provides valuable insight into contemporary Japanese critiques of Western modernity and the ideological mobilization for total war and austerity. Furthermore, the American consular officer's cover note provides an astute contemporary diplomatic observation, noting how Takata's thesis viewed Japan's European partners (Germany and Italy) essentially as expendable tools whose eventual downfall would accompany the general eclipse of the white race.
overview: This file consists of Despatch No. 170 (dated August 25, 1938) from the American Consulate General in Keijo (Seoul), Chosen (Korea), transmitting to the U.S. Secretary of State an English translation of an article titled 'Japanese People as Viewed from Natural Law of Rise and Fall of Nations' by Professor Tatsuma Takata of Kyoto University, published in the August 1938 issue of 'The Chosen and Manchu'. Takata presents a historical, demographic, and socioeconomic thesis arguing that the four-hundred-year global hegemony of the white European races is coming to an end due to plunging birth rates driven by excessive individualism and capitalist materialism. He contends that industrial capitalism inevitably spread modern production and military techniques to non-white nations, allowing Japan to achieve technological and military parity while maintaining lower production costs and stronger collective solidarity. Framing the ongoing conflict in China as an epochal struggle against Western powers backing China, Takata asserts Japan's historic mission to lead the colored races to global preeminence, cautioning the Japanese populace to reject Western living standards and embrace spiritual discipline and wartime austerity.

subfiles.about: Consular despatch transmitting an English translation of a Japanese magazine article predicting the shift of world leadership from the white to colored races.
subfiles.summary: The American Consulate General at Keijo transmits Despatch No. 170 to the Secretary of State in Washington, forwarding a translation of an article by Professor Tatsuma Takata of Kyoto University published in the August 1938 issue of 'The Chosen and Manchu'. The despatch notes the author's argument that global leadership is passing from the white race to the colored races under Japanese leadership. The consular officer highlights as particularly noteworthy the author's view of Japan's European allies, who appear to be regarded merely as instruments facilitating their own ultimate downfall.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 170 from American Consulate General, Keijo, transmitting translation of Japanese magazine article

subfiles.about: Academic magazine article analyzing the decline of European supremacy due to falling birth rates and individualism, and arguing that Japan is destined to lead the colored races to world leadership.
subfiles.from: Tatsuma Takata, Lit. D., Professor of Kyoto University
subfiles.summary: Professor Tatsuma Takata analyzes the historical rise and fall of civilizations, contending that the four-century dominance of European white nations is ending due to declining birth rates caused by excessive individualism, capitalist calculation, and social climbing. He argues that while Western capitalism initially enriched Europe through imperialist extraction, it inevitably disseminated industrial machinery and technical knowledge to non-Western peoples, enabling Japan to match the West in armament and technology while benefiting from lower production costs and social cohesion. Interpreting the Sino-Japanese conflict not merely as a localized struggle but as a transformative confrontation against Western colonial hegemony in Asia, Takata calls on the Japanese people to resist rising standards of living, maintain spiritual discipline, and embrace national austerity to fulfill Japan's world-historical destiny.
subfiles.title: Translation of article 'Japanese People as Viewed from Natural Law of Rise and Fall of Nations' by Tatsuma Takata
